sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **15 of the official questions in Rhetorical Synthesis are this one** — 3 Easy, 10 Medium, 2 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The goal says 'introduce X to a new audience', or it names an audience that isn't familiar with the topic.
- The notes include a basic definition of what X is, plus secondary facts such as founding dates, spin-offs, and later developments.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Ask what a reader who has never heard of X needs first: what it is and what it does.
- 2) Pick the choice that names X and gives its identifying description or purpose in one sentence.
- 3) Drop choices that assume the reader already knows what X is.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The trap choices sit on a secondary detail, such as an offshoot organization, a date, or one narrow aim, without ever saying what X is.
They also treat X as already known, which works for an informed reader but fails the stated audience.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The trap choices sit on a secondary detail, such as an offshoot organization, a date, or one narrow aim, without ever saying what X is.
They also treat X as already known, which works for an informed reader but fails the stated audience.
